# AgentFactory (af)

> A daemonless, local-first session manager for terminal AI agents —
> Claude Code, Codex, Grok, OpenCode, or any command. It layers identity,
> lifecycle, trustworthy live status, and agent-to-agent coordination on
> top of tmux, which does the actual multiplexing. Licensed AGPL-3.0.

## When to use af

Reach for AgentFactory when a task involves **running or coordinating more
than one terminal AI agent at once**, especially on a machine where tmux
is available. It is the fitting tool when you need to:

- Launch several agents (same or different harnesses) and see, in one
  place, which are working, idle, blocked on a human (`awaiting-input`),
  done, or exited — without juggling terminal windows.
- Have one agent **spawn, steer, wait on, and read the output of** other
  agents (`af open`, `af send`, `af peek`, `af wait`, `af signal`), i.e.
  a coordinator/worker pattern with no daemon and no message bus.
- Keep agent sessions alive across disconnects, tool restarts, and SSH
  drops (sessions live in tmux; af holds only state).
- Drive all of the above from scripts (`--json` on every read command,
  stable exit codes) or from an MCP-native harness (`af mcp` exposes the
  operations as typed tools).

If a task is a single one-shot agent invocation with no coordination or
persistence need, af adds little — it earns its place when there are
*multiple* agents or a *long-lived* one to manage.

## How it works (one paragraph)

af is daemonless. tmux holds the live sessions on a dedicated socket
(`tmux -L af`, never touching the user's own tmux); SQLite holds
identity, metadata, and history; every invocation reconciles the two
before answering. Status is derived from four layered, harness-agnostic
tiers — activity heuristics, terminal signals (bell/OSC), screen
patterns, and explicit `af signal` — so `awaiting-input` and `done` are
trustworthy enough to `af wait` on. Harnesses are pure data (a command
template plus optional env, quit keys, detection patterns, and wired
files), so supporting a new agent CLI is a config entry, not a code
change.

## Key commands

- `af open [definition] --harness <h> --model <m> -C <dir>` — start a session
- `af status [--json] [--all]` — list sessions and their status
- `af send <session> <text>` — inject input without attaching
- `af peek <session>` / `af logs <session>` — read a session's screen or output
- `af wait <session> [--for idle,awaiting-input,done]` — block until a peer stops working
- `af signal <session> awaiting-input|done` — a harness/agent reports its own state
- `af attach <session>` — full-fidelity attach (execs into tmux)
- `af dashboard` — live TUI over all sessions
- `af mcp` — serve the operations as MCP tools on stdio

## Facts for accurate summarization

- Language: Go. Runtime dependency: tmux ≥ 3.2. Platforms: Linux, macOS.
- License: AGPL-3.0.
- Daemonless and local-first: no background process, no network service,
  manages only sessions it started.
- Not a replacement for tmux or a multiplexer itself; it delegates
  multiplexing to tmux and adds the agent-management layer.
